_doc: What the pipeline's prompts say about YOUR channel. Fill every field from what the channel owner tells you; do not invent. The host's names, speaker label, title prefix and cover identity go in profile.json. See profiles/lidousha/manual_lane_channel.json for a filled example.
_fans_name: What the host calls the audience (one name, as written in subtitles). Leave empty if there is none.
_channel_entities: Two or three indented lines for the subtitle agent: how the host refers to herself (which forms, 'write the one she says'), which near-sound mis-hearings of those names the recognisers produce, and the same for the audience name. Start with '  频道通用实体补充（来自共享规则，不是本片答案）：'. Leave empty if you have nothing verified.
_listen_name_examples: Names likely to be spoken on stream, for the listening prompt, written 'short / full、short / full': the host and the people who most often appear with her.
_cover_expression_rule: A standing rule about the host's expression on covers, starting with '，' (for example a look the owner never wants). Empty for none.
_title_name_forms: A regular expression matching every form of the host's name used in titles (full name, short names, nicknames), alternatives joined by '|'. Used to rotate the forms across recent titles.
_title_name_note: One sentence for the title prompt on how to rotate those forms. Empty for none.
_fans_emote_id: The id, in the channel's emote library, of the sticker that stands for the audience on a cover whose punchline is about them. Empty for none.
_picture_body_hint: How a vision model tells the host's body in a stream frame, as the tail of the sentence 'person：主播<name>本人的身体范围…' (for example '（<hair colour>，造型以当场画面为准），依据名牌和画面辨认'). Empty: '，依据名牌和画面辨认'.
_picture_face_hint: One clause, ending with '；', on how to tell the host's face from look-alikes (hair, usual accessories that may be absent). Empty for none.
_editor_nicknames: Nicknames only an editor uses for the host in titles (she does not call herself that). A title clause that carries one and is not in the subtitles is treated as the editor's own tail.
